injuries.shortComment: Beck (back) was listed as a non-participant on Thursday's injury report, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Beck thus appears to be trending toward a second straight absence Sunday against the Commanders due to the back spasms that flared up late last week. If the Cardinals ultimately rule out Beck on Friday's practice report, Josh Johnson again will be under center for Arizona this weekend.

injuries.shortComment: Slovis was claimed off waivers by the Cardinals on Wednesday, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN reports.
injuries.longComment: Slovis had been waived by the Ravens earlier in the week, and while the team hoped to bring him back, the equally quarterback-embattled Cardinals swooped in and claimed him. With that, Slovis returns to the team he played for in 2025.

injuries.shortComment: Head coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday that the Cardinals will evaluate Love (ankle) again Monday to hone in on a return date for the running back, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Love must miss at least one more game due to the right high-ankle sprain that he picked up in a Week 8 win at Dallas, but the Cardinals have a decision to make next week, as they have a Week 13 matchup with the Eagles on tap before a Week 14 bye. For as long as Love is sidelined, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will continue to man Arizona's backfield.

injuries.shortComment: Head coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday that Johnson is preparing to start Sunday's game versus the Commanders due to Carson Beck's back injury, Dani Sureck of the Cardinals' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Beck won't practice Wednesday due to continued issues with back spasms, which held him out of this past Sunday's loss in Kansas City. In place of Beck, Johnson completed 18 of 31 passes for 155 yards and one touchdown while also taking two carries for five yards. Friday's injury report will reveal if Beck has a chance to play in Week 12, and by proxy if Johnson will get another spot start.

injuries.shortComment: Gibbens registered 10 total tackles (six solo) during Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.
injuries.longComment: Gibbens was able to lead the team in takedowns in Week 11, recording double-digit tackles for the second time in four weeks. The linebacker has now compiled 76 total tackles (33 solo), including 0.5 sacks, while also notching a pass defensed over 11 contests so far this season.

injuries.shortComment: Baker recorded six total tackles (five solo) during Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City.
injuries.longComment: Baker was able to register at least six stops for the fourth week in a row and seventh time overall this year. The safety is about as steady as they come, compiling 74 total tackles (36 solo), including a career-high 3.5 sacks, while also adding an interception and a forced fumble over 11 contests so far during the 2026 season.

injuries.shortComment: Wilson recorded eight total tackles (four solo) during Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.
injuries.longComment: Wilson was able to register at least eight stops for the second straight week and fifth time overall this season. The linebacker has now compiled 80 total tackles (35 solo), two passes defensed and a forced fumble over 11 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

injuries.shortComment: Duvernay logged 81 kickoff-return yards in the Cardinals' 34-7 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Duvernay played two offensive snaps and nine special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The wide receiver took a step back after drawing three targets in Week 10, as both Simi Fehoko and Harrison Wallace were clearly ahead of him Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Virgil wasn't targeted in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.
injuries.longComment: The 22-year-old wide receiver played just two offensive snaps, the same amount as Devin Duvernay, as the duo played behind all three of Simi Fehoko (52 snaps), Harrison Wallace (36) and Zay Jones (32) in the Cardinals' injury-ravaged wideout depth chart. Virgil has three catches for 54 yards on 11 targets across seven games this season and therefore doesn't possess any fantasy relevance at the moment.

injuries.shortComment: Higgins caught his lone target for four yards during the Cardinals' 34-7 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: The Cardinals offense struggled Sunday with Josh Johnson as the starter in the absence of Carson Beck (back). Of Johnson's 31 pass attempts, 26 of them were split between Trey McBride (14), Harrison Wallace (seven) and Simi Fehoko (five), leaving very little for Higgins and the other Cardinals pass catchers. Higgins has only one catch over his last two outings and a 19-166-1 line on 21 targets through 11 regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Fehoko caught one of five targets for a two-yard touchdown in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.
injuries.longComment: The wideout led his position group by playing 52 of 56 offensive snaps, and he ran a team-high 34 routes on Josh Johnson's 37 dropbacks. It didn't translate to much production outside of the short touchdown, as Fehoko has consistently shown he can't win enough as an NFL receiver. He's been thrust into heavy snaps due to a litany of injuries in Arizona. Fehoko can mostly be ignored in fantasy until he shows something more in the box score.

injuries.shortComment: Jones reverted to the Cardinals' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
injuries.longComment: Jones' 32 snaps on offense during Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs were ahead of both Devin Duvernay and Reggie Virgil (two each) and behind Simi Fehoko (52) and Harrison Wallace (36). Jones finished the game with a one-yard carry and a 17-yard catch on two targets, and that reception ended up being the second-longest offensive play for the Cardinals. Given his usage in Week 11, Jones stands a good chance of being brought up for Week 12 against the Commanders on Nov. 29, although his next elevation from the practice squad is the last one he is eligible for this season.

injuries.shortComment: Wallace finished Sunday's loss to Kansas City with four catches for 57 yards on seven targets.
injuries.longComment: Wallace began the season on the Cardinals' practice squad and didn't play in his first NFL game until Week 9 versus Seattle. After logging a total of seven offensive snaps and one catch across his first two contests, the rookie paced Arizona wideouts in targets, receptions and receiving yards. Wallace also ranked second among the wideout corps with 36 offensive snaps, so it appears there was a conscious effort to involve him in the team's passing game. The Cardinals' wide-receiver room has lacked a reliable option since Michael Wilson went down with a season-ending neck injury, so the door is wide open for Wallace to claim a prominent role with continued production.

injuries.shortComment: Ryland made his lone extra-point attempt in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.
injuries.longComment: Playing with their third- and fourth-string quarterbacks, the Cardinals have mustered a total of 13 points over their last two games. Ryland has minimal fantasy appeal in an offense struggling to simply move the ball. On the season, he's 22-for-24 on field-goal tries and 17-for-18 on PATs across 11 games.

injuries.shortComment: Quitoriano played all 13 of his snaps on special teams in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.
injuries.longComment: Since coming out of nowhere to post two receiving touchdowns in his Cardinals debut back in Week 5 against the Lions, Quitoriano has fallen out of the mix for playing time on offense. After the two-score effort, Quitoriano logged double-digit snaps on offense in four straight contests, but he drew just one target over that stretch. In the subsequent two games, Quitoriano has played just three total snaps on offense while Trey McBride, Elijah Higgins and Hunter Long have been prioritized ahead of him at tight end.

injuries.shortComment: Knight carried the ball seven times for 35 yards and caught his only target for 10 yards in Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City.
injuries.longComment: Although he split the backfield workload nearly equally with Tyler Allgeier, Knight was the more productive RB, although he still failed to reach 50 rushing yards for a fourth straight game. The 25-year-old running back gets a more favorable matchup in Week 12 against the Commanders, but Knight and Allgeier could face additional competition for touches if Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is cleared to return.

injuries.shortComment: Allgeier carried the ball seven times for 23 yards in Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City.
injuries.longComment: Game script fairly quickly put the Cardinals' running game in mothballs, and Allgeier wound up splitting the backfield workload nearly equally with Bam Knight, who picked up 45 scrimmage yards on eight touches. Allgeier has gone three straight games without reaching 50 rushing yards or getting into the end zone, but those games were also against very tough opponents (the Seahawks in Week 9 and the Rams in Week 10). The fifth-year RB could find a little more running room in Week 12 against the Commanders, but Jeremiyah Love (ankle) might also be ready to rejoin the lineup by then.

injuries.shortComment: McBride caught nine of 14 targets for 54 yards in Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City. He added four yards on his only carry.
injuries.longComment: Working with his fourth quarterback of the season in Josh Johnson, McBride dominated the 40-year-old's attention, as no other Cardinal got more than seven targets or hauled in more than four passes. The star tight end wasn't able to do much with the volume, however, as his longest gain went for a mere nine yards. Carson Beck (back) could be back under center in Week 12 against the Commanders, but that might not improve McBride's outlook, as he saw only five targets in Week 10 during the rookie QB's first NFL start.

injuries.shortComment: Simon (calf) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
injuries.longComment: Simon is being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's contest. His absence gives the Cardinals less depth at linebacker behind Jack Gibbens, Mack Wilson and Zaven Collins.

injuries.shortComment: Pearce (back) practiced in full Thursday, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Pearce was listed as a limited participant Wednesday but was able to practice without limitations one day later. As such, he should be good to go for Sunday's matchup in Minnesota.

injuries.shortComment: Daniels (Achilles) was limited during Thursday's practice, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Daniels has been dealing with an Achilles issue since late October, but is hasn't yet caused him to miss any games. With that in mind, unless he's suffered a setback, Daniels seems likely to suit up Sunday in Minnesota. He's had a solid rookie season, tallying 69 tackles, including 1.0 sacks, two defensed passes (including an interception) and one fumble recovery through 10 contests.

injuries.shortComment: Dotson (hamstring) did not participate in Thursday's practice, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: It's the second straight missed practice for Dotson, who is dealing with a hamstring issue. That's not a good sign ahead of Sunday's Week 12 clash against Minnesota, but Dotson will have one more chance to get on the practice field Friday. If he ends up being sidelined Sunday, Olamide Zaccheaus could take on a larger offensive snap share, as could Zachariah Branch, though he's also looking iffy to suit up due to a hamstring issue of his own.

injuries.shortComment: Deablo (forearm) was not listed on Wednesday's injury report, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Deablo aggravated a forearm injury against the Bengals in Week 9, which prevented him from playing against the Chiefs in Week 10. He's had additional time to recover courtesy of the bye, and given his absence from Wednesday's injury report, Deablo is on track to play against the Vikings on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Branch (hamstring) didn't participate in Wednesday's practice, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: After being sidelined for the Falcons' previous two games, Branch isn't yet back to full health coming out of a Week 11 bye. The Falcons will see what, if anything, Branch is able to do at practices Thursday and Friday before deciding whether he'll carry a designation into Sunday's game against the Vikings. The rookie third-round pick out of Georgia has been a regular presence on the Falcons' return units but hasn't seen much involvement on offense when healthy; he's recorded 10 catches for 64 yards on 12 targets through his first eight NFL appearances.

injuries.shortComment: Zaccheaus caught two of his four targets for 17 yards and returned five punts for 81 yards during Atlanta's loss Sunday versus the Chiefs.
injuries.longComment: Zaccheaus recorded a season-high 17 receiving yards during the loss while playing 29 snaps on offense and 14 on special teams. The 29-year-old has hauled in eight passes for 43 yards in addition to amassing 231 kick-return yards and 81 punt-return yards across nine games this season.

injuries.shortComment: Herbert caught two of his three targets for seven yards during Sunday's 35-13 loss versus the Chiefs. He also returned six kickoffs for 168 yards.
injuries.longComment: Herbert was targeted three times for the second straight game in Week 10, but he continued to make a bigger impact on special teams. His first kickoff return of the day went for 39 yards to Atlanta's 45-yard line, but the offense promptly went three and out. He'll be hoping to keep up the momentum as a returner following the Falcons' bye in Week 11.

injuries.shortComment: Moody went 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs.
injuries.longComment: Moody was signed by the Falcons off the Ravens' practice squad Tuesday, and he was able to put together a perfect debut with the team in Week 10. The kicker converted a 28-yard field-goal try in the second quarter before later adding a 38-yard make in the fourth. With Atlanta's bye week in Week 11, Moody's next chance to build on Sunday's performance will come in Week 12 against the Vikings.

injuries.shortComment: Hooper recorded an eight-yard reception on his lone target in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs.
injuries.longComment: Hooper was on the field for just 11 of the Falcons' 72 offensive snaps, with his 15 percent share placing him comfortably behind Kyle Pitts (76 percent) and Charlie Woerner (44 percent) among Atlanta tight ends. The 32-year-old Hooper hasn't played more than half of the snaps in any of Atlanta's first 10 games and has turned in a 10-84-1 receiving line on 12 targets, a level of production that keeps him well off the fantasy radar.

injuries.shortComment: Head coach Kevin Stefanski said Monday that London was cleared of a concussion near the end of Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: London was checked for a possible concussion in the fourth quarter of Week 10 action, but the result of the evaluation wasn't reported before the game concluded. Prior to his exit Sunday, he posted his third 100-yard game (109, to be exact) of the campaign on six catches and a season-high 12 targets. London will continue to operate as the Falcons' No. 1 WR after a Week 11 bye in the team's next game Sunday, Nov. 29, at Minnesota.

injuries.shortComment: Penix completed 23 of 43 passes for 286 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and rushed four times for 29 yards in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered.
injuries.longComment: Penix struggled while the game was still in question, but he did manage to pad his stats some down the stretch as the Falcons unsuccessfully tried to overcome their deficit. Penix connected with eight different targets overall on the afternoon, and he ultimately finished with a season high in passing yards. Penix has now tossed six interceptions in the last three games, however, and he'll look to regroup during the Week 11 bye before tackling a difficult matchup against the Vikings on the road on Sunday, Nov. 29.

injuries.shortComment: Pitts brought in four of five targets for 50 yards in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
injuries.longComment: The veteran tight end had a slow start to the day before coming on when the Falcons went especially pass-heavy in the second half. Pitts' fumble, his first of the season, came with just over four minutes remaining in the game after the contest was out of reach, and his catch total was his highest since Week 7. Pitts remains a key complementary option in an Atlanta passing attack that's scuffled of late, and he'll look to bounce back after the Falcons emerge from a Week 11 bye with a Week 12 road matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.

injuries.shortComment: Robinson rushed 16 times for 71 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of five targets for six yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: The Falcons were down 14-3 by halftime and 21-3 doing into the final period, so Robinson's opportunities progressively dwindled due to game script. However, the star running back still averaged a solid 4.4 yards per carry and recorded his sixth rushing touchdown of the season on a three-yard run in the fourth quarter. Robinson has at least four receptions in three of the last four games, and he'll now have a Week 11 bye to rest up before a tough Week 12 road matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.

injuries.shortComment: Green (knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
injuries.longComment: Green's practice reps were limited Wednesday due to a knee injury, but his full session Thursday puts him on track to play against the Texans on Sunday. The second-year edge rusher has accumulated 32 tackles (20 solo), including 7.5 sacks, across 11 regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Hawkins (knee) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Hawkins was held out of Wednesday's practice due to a lingering knee injury, which has prevented him from playing in each of the Ravens' last five games. However, a full session Friday could be enough for Hawkins to avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans.

injuries.shortComment: Bateman (groin) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Bateman was limited in Wednesday's session due to a groin injury, but his full practice Thursday puts the sixth-year wide receiver on track to play against the Texans on Sunday. He hauled in his second touchdown of the year in a Week 11 loss to the Panthers and is up to a 25-403-2 receiving line on 42 targets through 11 regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Flowers (ankle) was listed as a full participant in Thursday's practice.
injuries.longComment: Flowers was limited at practice Wednesday, but the wide receiver's quick return to all activity one day later clears the way for him to suit up Sunday against the Texans. In his last outing, Flowers (who has recorded a fantasy-friendly 57-785-3 line on 82 targets through 10 games), was on the field for 88 percent of his team's snaps on offense in a 35-33 loss to the Panthers in Week 11 en route to catching eight of his game-high 11 targets for 97 yards.

injuries.shortComment: Henry (concussion) was listed as a full participant in Thursday's practice.
injuries.longComment: After logging a limited listing Wednesday, Henry's upgrade to 'full' Thursday has him trending in the right direction as Sunday's game against the Texans approaches. Either way, Friday's final injury report will dictate whether or not the Ravens' lead back carries an injury designation heading into the weekend.

injuries.shortComment: Humphrey (personal) was back at practice Wednesday and was a full participant, Quentin Corpuel of the Ravens' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Humphrey was a healthy inactive for Week 11 against the Panthers after making negative comments about the city of Baltimore on his podcast. It's unclear whether he'll play against the Texans on Sunday, with head coach Jesse Minter telling reporters Monday that the Ravens will make a decision about Humphrey's availability by the end of the week.

injuries.shortComment: Madubuike (hamstring) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Madubuike was unable to play against the Panthers in Week 11 due to a hamstring injury that he sustained against the Chargers in Week 10. He would need to practice in at least a limited capacity over the next two days to have a realistic shot at playing against the Texans on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Jones recorded eight tackles (five solo) including 1.0 sacks during Sunday's 35-33 loss at Carolina.
injuries.longComment: Jones got his first sack of the season in Week 11, and his eight total tackles were a career high. He should retain a big role on the interior of the Ravens' defensive line in a Week 12 tilt at Houston, and he'll be looking to keep up the momentum in that contest.

injuries.shortComment: Simpson recorded 10 total tackles (five solo) during Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.
injuries.longComment: Simpson was able to secure his first double-digit tackle performance of the year, leading the team in takedowns in Week 11. The linebacker has now compiled a career-high 75 total tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also intercepting a pass and recovering a fumble over 11 contests so far during the 2026 season.

injuries.shortComment: Hamilton recorded eight total tackles (five solo) during Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.
injuries.longComment: Hamilton was able to notch at least eight takedowns for the second week in a row and fourth time this season. The safety has now registered 78 total tackles (55 solo) and five passes defensed, including an interception, while also forcing a fumble over 11 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

injuries.shortComment: Smith recorded nine tackles (two solo) in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.
injuries.longComment: Smith has at least eight tackles in 10 of 11 games this season but has just two games with double-digit tackles. On the season, the veteran linebacker has piled up 91 tackles (40 solo), including 2.0 sacks, four pass breakups, including an interception, and two forced fumbles on 94 percent of the defensive snaps.

injuries.shortComment: Cuevas caught one of three targets for eight yards during Sunday's 35-33 loss at Carolina.
injuries.longComment: Cuevas continues to draw targets at an impressive clip, tallying three for his second straight game despite only being on the field for 14 of the Ravens' 61 offensive snaps in Week 11. Barring an injury to starter Mark Andrews or rookie fourth-rounder Matt Hibner, though, his role isn't big enough to warrant fantasy consideration in most formats. Baltimore will take on the Texans in Week 12.

injuries.shortComment: Lane didn't garner a target during Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.
injuries.longComment: Lane failed to reel in a pass for the second time in three weeks, and both times the ball was thrown his way Sunday, the play was negated by a defensive penalty, resulting in no targets for the rookie. He was on the field for 33 offensive snaps, ranking third at wide receiver for Baltimore behind Rashod Bateman (59) and Zay Flowers (57). Lane's next chance to get back on track will come in Week 12 against the Texans.

injuries.shortComment: Walker recorded 211 kickoff-return yards, including an 86-yard touchdown, and one catch for 34 yards in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.
injuries.longComment: The wide receiver filled a returner role for the first time this season and did well. Walker has seen just 10 targets on offense in 2026, so he's not much of a factor in fantasy leagues at the moment, but he could garner more opportunities on special teams following Sunday's success.

injuries.shortComment: Patterson made his only field-goal attempt and went 4-for-4 on extra-point tries during Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.
injuries.longComment: Patterson was able to convert his only field-goal try in Week 11, nailing a chip-shot 28-yard attempt in the first quarter. He's now combined to go 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts while making all six of his PATs over two contests as the starting kicker for Baltimore, and he likely will remain in that role for Week 12 with Tyler Loop (groin) sidelined for at least one more contest.

injuries.shortComment: Hibner recorded two catches for 12 yards on two targets in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.
injuries.longComment: Hibner logged 35 of 65 snaps on offense, with his 54 percent share ranking second to only Mark Andrews (62 percent) among Ravens tight ends. The rookie fourth-round pick out of SMU's playing time has held steady between 30 and 60 percent of snaps over his 10 appearances, with Hibner drawing no more than two targets in any of those contests.

injuries.shortComment: Andrews caught two of three targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 35-33 loss to Carolina.
injuries.longComment: While the veteran tight end showed some instant chemistry with new quarterback Jacoby Brissett last week, Andrews saw his target volume crater in their second game together, as rookie depth TEs Josh Cuevas and Matthew Hibner saw similar usage as pass catchers. Andrews has failed to reach 25 receiving yards in five of his last six games and hasn't scored a TD in seven straight contests, making him a very risky fantasy option in Week 12 against the Texans.

injuries.shortComment: Hill carried the ball six times for 69 yards and a touchdown and caught four of five targets for 27 yards in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.
injuries.longComment: Derrick Henry had a strong performance as well but was knocked out of the game in the fourth quarter and got checked for a concussion. Hill was heavily involved in the offense prior to that, however, scoring from 19 yards out in the late in the second quarter. He almost had a second TD earlier in the quarter, but Hill had the ball punched loose at the one-yard line after a 36-yard scamper and saw it bounce out of the end zone for a turnover and a touchback. Henry cleared the concussion protocol after the game and figures to be active in the Week 12 against the Texans, but Hill's usage appears to be on the upswing as the Ravens' No. 2 back.

injuries.shortComment: Brissett completed 24 of 37 passes for 276 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers. He added seven rushing yards on two carries.
injuries.longComment: It was another decent showing for the veteran quarterback, and his first TD pass in two games as a Raven came on a trick that involved a direct snap to Derrick Henry, who flipped it Brissett for a 52-yard strike to Rashod Bateman. Brissett has also kept Zay Flowers relevant, feeding the wideout 18 targets for a 14-171-0 line. Baltimore's passing attack will try to keep improving in Week 12 against the Texans.

injuries.shortComment: Shakir brought in three of six targets for 33 yards in the Bills' 13-10 in over the Chiefs on Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Shakir's reception and yardage totals led the Bills on a night when Josh Allen threw for just 81 yards with a pair of picks. The veteran slot receiver was coming off a Week 11 showing against the Dolphins in which he accrued a season-high 101 receiving yards, and Thursday's downturn was largely explainable by Allen's struggles and less-than-ideal weather conditions. Shakir should remain a key target for Allen during a Week 13 road matchup Sunday, Dec. 6 with a Patriots squad that the wideout posted a 7-82-0 line against back in Week 4.

injuries.shortComment: Moore hauled in two of six targets for 15 yards in the Bills' 13-10 win over the Chiefs on Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Moore's production, like that of the rest of his fellow skill-position players, was very modest on a night when Josh Allen threw for only 81 yards and a pair of interceptions. The talented wideout's catch and yardage totals were both his third-lowest tallies of the season, but Moore is still averaging a formidable 14.6 yards per reception heading into a Week 13 road matchup against the Patriots on Sunday, Dec. 6.

injuries.shortComment: Kincaid brought in both targets for 13 yards in the Bills' 13-10 loss to the Chiefs on Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Making his return from a one-game absence due to thumb and ankle injuries, Kincaid's numbers weren't quite as poor within the context of a night where Josh Allen threw for only 81 yards and completed less than 50.0 percent of his passes. Kincaid tied for runner-up slotting on the Bills in receptions, and he was third in receiving yards as well. Kincaid now has multiple catches in five straight games heading into a Week 13 road divisional matchup against the Patriots on Sunday, Dec. 6.

injuries.shortComment: Allen completed 10 of 21 passes for 81 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions and added seven carries for 43 yards in the Bills' 13-10 win over the Chiefs on Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Allen's abysmal numbers tell the tale of how difficult a night it was for the star signal-caller under less-than-ideal weather conditions and while facing a talented veteran defense. Allen's passing yardage total was a season low, and the two-interception  tally was his second straight. Allen also took a pair of sacks and completed a season-worst 47.6 percent of his passes, but he helped bring Buffalo back from a 10-7 fourth-quarter deficit. Allen's lackluster showing aside, he'll remain an elite option in all formats for a Week 13 road divisional clash against the Patriots on Sunday, Dec. 6.

injuries.shortComment: Cook rushed 32 times for 117 yards and a touchdown and brought in his only target for eight yards in the Bills' 13-10 win over the Chiefs on Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Cook logged a season high in rush attempts while eclipsing the century mark for the third time in the last four games. Cook's longest gain went for only 10 yards, so he worked hard for everything he got against a tough Chiefs front. Cook added his 11th rushing touchdown of the season on a five-yard run early in the second quarter, and he'll have some extra recovery time before he takes aim at the Patriots defense in a Week 13 road matchup on Sunday, Dec. 6.

injuries.shortComment: Sanders (shoulder) is active for Thursday's game against Kansas City.
injuries.longComment: Sanders has been officially cleared to return from a one-game absence due to a shoulder injury, and his presence means DeWayne Carter will revert to a rotational role at defensive end for Thanksgiving Day. Sanders has 11 tackles (five solo) through five regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Williams (calf) is active for Thursday's game against the Chiefs.
injuries.longComment: Williams didn't play against the Dolphins in Week 11 due to a calf injury, but the fourth-year pro has been cleared by medical staff to play Thursday. He has accumulated 61 tackles (27 solo), including 1.0 sacks, four pass defenses (including two interceptions) and one fumble recovery across nine regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Benford (groin) is inactive for Thursday's game against the Chiefs.
injuries.longComment: Benford will end up missing a second consecutive game due to a groin injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the Jets. Maxwell Hairston should see a bump in defensive snaps at outside cornerback in the absence of Benford, whose next chance to play is Week 13 against the Patriots on Sunday, Dec. 6.

injuries.shortComment: Rousseau (back) was a full participant in Tuesday's walkthrough practice.
injuries.longComment: Rousseau was limited in Monday's session while managing a back injury, but his full participation Tuesday indicates that the sixth-year edge rusher will be available against the Chiefs on Thanksgiving Day. Rousseau logged two sacks against the Dolphins on Sunday, and his 10.0 sacks through 10 regular-season games are second-most in the NFL behind Will Anderson (11.5).

injuries.shortComment: Hooker logged two solo tackles and one pass defensed in the Bills' 26-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Hooker has now played in two games for the Bills, logging 100 percent of the team's defensive reps in Week 11 and 98 percent in Week 12. The strong safety has made for a good pairing with Cole Bishop, and the duo has helped the Bills' defense extend its streak of not allowing a touchdown to 15 straight quarters of play.

injuries.shortComment: Bernard logged two tackles (one solo) in the Bills' 26-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Bernard had his lowest output of the season in Sunday's contest. The linebacker played 28 defensive snaps, equating to 62 percent of the team's defensive plays. The defensive captain was likely pulled early to rest for Thursday night's primetime game against the Chiefs.

injuries.shortComment: Shavers failed to bring in either of his two targets and logged one tackle on kick coverage in the Bills' 26-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Shavers played 27 offensive snaps and 16 special-teams in his return to the field Sunday. The wide receiver has finally started to mix into the offense after recovering from the torn ACL he suffered in the Bills' 27-24 wild-card win over the Jaguars last January.

injuries.shortComment: Johnson rushed once for two yards and caught seven of his eight targets for 55 yards in the Bills' 26-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Johnson did not carry the rock much at all in the contest. The running back did, however, rank third in receiving yards for Buffalo behind Khalil Shakir (101) and DJ Moore (91). Johnson should continue to see receiving opportunities in Week 12 against the Chiefs as the Bills' preferred third-down back.

injuries.shortComment: Latu recorded a 30-yard reception on four targets in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.
injuries.longComment: With Dalton Kincaid (thumb) inactive, Latu moved a rung up on the ladder at tight end and ended up seeing his most extensive playing time on offense of the season, logging 28 of 78 snaps (36 percent). He parlayed the elevated snaps into a season-high target count, but Latu's lone reception actually came on special teams, when Tommy Doman faked a punt and connected with the 24-year-old deep down the field for a fourth-down conversion. Latu will likely see his opportunities take a hit if Kincaid makes it back for a Thursday matchup with the Chiefs in Week 12.

injuries.shortComment: Bass went 4-for-5 on field-goal tries and made both of his PATs during Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.
injuries.longComment: Bass was able to make at least three field goals for the fifth time in the team's last six contests. The kicker made field goals from 43 and 54 yards in the first half before adding makes from 40 and 28 yards in the fourth quarter. His lone miss of the day came in the third quarter, when he pulled a 54-yard try wide left, registering his first missed field-goal try of the year. Bass has now gone 24-for-25 on field-goal attempts, including 4-for-5 from 50-plus yards, over 10 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

injuries.shortComment: Coleman caught two of four targets for 17 yards during Sunday's 26-9 win over Miami.
injuries.longComment: Coleman finished with fewer than 20 receiving yards for the fourth straight week, and he hasn't reached the end zone since Week 6. The wide receiver has operated in a limited role on offense since DJ Moore returned to action in Week 8 following a shoulder injury, and Coleman will remain an unattractive fantasy asset ahead of the team's matchup with the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night.

injuries.shortComment: Davis rushed one time for three yards and caught a six-yard pass on two targets in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.
injuries.longComment: Even with the Bills having a quick Week 12 turnaround ahead of Thursday night's game against the Chiefs on Thanksgiving, Buffalo rode James Cook and handed him 22 carries rather than spelling him a little more ahead of a short week. Davis has handled 17 carries across 10 games this season, turning them into a measly 55 yards and no touchdowns. His only fantasy value is being Cook's backup.

injuries.shortComment: Okereke (foot) was listed as a non-participant in Carolina's practice estimate Thursday, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Okereke is in danger of missing a third consecutive game as he continues to deal with a knee injury suffered during Week 8. If he ends up being unable to play in Monday's matchup versus the Buccaneers, Tyrel Dodson will likely get another start at inside linebacker.

injuries.shortComment: Evans (Achilles) was listed as a DNP on Thursday's estimated practice report, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Evans may have picked up the injury during the Panthers' 35-33 win over the Ravens this past Sunday, when he caught all five of his targets for 44 yards, which included a 23-yard grab in the first quarter. Given that the Panthers didn't practice Thanksgiving Day, Evans' practice participation over the next two days will be worth monitoring ahead of Monday's game against the Buccaneers.

injuries.shortComment: Tremble (knee) was listed as a limited participant on Thursday's estimated practice report, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Tremble was cleared to play through a knee injury against the Ravens in Week 11, when he hauled in his lone target for 18 yards while playing 59 of 71 offensive snaps (83.1 percent) in a 35-33 win for the Panthers. Carolina did not practice Thanksgiving Day, so Tremble's participation over the next two days will provide clarity on his status ahead of Monday's NFC South showdown against Tampa Bay.

injuries.shortComment: Brooks (groin) was estimated as a full practice participant on Thursday's report, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: The Panthers didn't practice Thursday for Thanksgiving, so the report provided by the team was an estimation. Given that, Brooks' practice participation over the next two days will provide a better indication of his status heading into Monday's NFC South tilt against the Buccaneers. However, Brooks would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Week 12. The third-year running back landed on IR in late September after undergoing surgery to repair a core-muscle injury that he sustained against the Falcons in Week 2.

injuries.shortComment: Waller (knee) was listed as limited on Thursday's estimated injury report, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: For s second week in a row, Waller is dealing with a knee injury, but his listing to begin this week implies he's a bit healthier after kicking off Week 11 prep with a DNP. He'll have two more opportunities to practice in full Friday and Saturday before the Panthers potentially make a call on his status for Monday's game at Tampa Bay.

injuries.shortComment: McMillan (foot) was listed as a DNP on Thursday's practice estimate, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: After McMillan didn't participate in Wednesday's unofficial practice due to a sore foot, head coach Dave Canales told Kaye that the team is "optimistic" that the wide receiver will play Monday at Tampa Bay. McMillan will have two more chances to mix into drills this week before the Panthers potentially tag him with a designation for Week 12 action.

injuries.shortComment: The Panthers designated Incoom (calf) to return from injured reserve Wednesday, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Incoom was placed on injured reserve in late October due to a calf injury that he sustained in Week 6 against the Eagles. Regardless of his practice participation over the next three days, the Panthers would have to activate Incoom from injured reserve in order for him to be available for Monday's NFC South tilt against the Buccaneers.

injuries.shortComment: Dodson tallied eight tackles (five solo), an interception and a fumble recovery during Carolina's win over the Ravens on Sunday,
injuries.longComment: Dodson came up big for the Panthers in the win, forcing two turnovers, including a game-clinching  interception of Jacoby Brissett late in the fourth quarter. The 28-year-old has now totaled seven or more tackles in three consecutive games and he will look to maintain this level of production during the Week 12 matchup versus the Buccaneers.

injuries.shortComment: Christensen (hamstring) reverted to season-ending injured reserve after his 21-day practice window closed Tuesday, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Christensen has been rehabbing from a hamstring injury all year, but he was not activated from IR within 21 days of returning to practice, so he'll now miss the rest of the season. The veteran guard will now have to look forward to hopefully returning at some point in 2027.

injuries.shortComment: Lloyd recorded four tackles (two solo) in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.
injuries.longComment: The four tackles matched Lloyd's season low in a game this season, which he's done three times in nine contests. While he doesn't post huge tackle numbers, Lloyd makes noise in other areas of the box score. He's piled up 67 tackles (39 solo), including 2.5 sacks, and five pass breakups, including three interceptions, on 94 percent of the defensive snaps in 2026.

injuries.shortComment: Legette did not play an offensive snap in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.
injuries.longComment: The wide receiver did play nine snaps on special teams. Legette missed six games with a knee injury before returning for Carolina's win over the Saints in Week 10, though he only saw action on two offensive snaps in that contest. Legette has two catches for 64 yards and no touchdowns in four games this season.

injuries.shortComment: Metchie caught one of three targets for 19 yards during the Panthers' 35-33 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Metchie and Bryce Young connected on a 19-yard pass late in the third quarter to set the Panthers up in the red zone, and the drive ended four plays later on a 33-yard field goal by Ryan Fitzgerald. Metchie has caught one pass in each of his last two outings, and the fifth-year pro is firmly behind Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker on the wide-receiver depth chart. The Panthers will hit the road in Week 12 for a crucial NFC South clash against the Buccaneers on Monday, Nov. 30.

injuries.shortComment: Etienne rushed six times for 29 yards, caught one pass for seven yards, logged 36 kickoff-return yards and recorded eight punt-return yards in the Panthers' 35-33 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Etienne did it all in Week 11 while only playing 10 offensive snaps and nine special-teams snaps. Despite the modest playing time, the running back made an impact across the box score. Etienne continues to be the reserve option behind bell-cow back Chuba Hubbard, whose role is as entrenched as any player at his position in the league.

injuries.shortComment: Fitzgerald went 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made all three of his PATs during Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.
injuries.longComment: Fitzgerald was able to make multiple field-goal tries for the second straight week and seventh time overall this season. The kicker made a 33-yard field goal in the third quarter before he converted a 37-yarder with 1:44 left in the fourth quarter, ultimately putting the Panthers in front 35-33. Fitzgerald now has gone 17-for-19 on field-goal attempts, including 5-for-5 from 50-plus yards, while converting 21 of 26 extra-point tries over 10 contests so far during the 2026 season.

injuries.shortComment: Horn is progressing well in his recovery from a quadriceps injury, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Horn is currently considered day-to-day, but head coach Dave Canales wants to ensure Horn is in a great head space before returning. The 2021 first-round pick has been sidelined since late September, while Chau Smith-Wade has handled slot-cornerback duties in his absence. The Panthers will still have to officially activate Horn off injured reserve before he's eligible to return.

injuries.shortComment: Hrad coach Dave Canales said Monday that Coker has been cleared from the concussion protocol, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Coker endured a helmet-to-helmet hit at the end of a six-yard catch in the fourth quarter of Sunday's win against the Ravens, getting shaken up in the process. Afterward, be reportedly entered the concussion protocol, but one day later he doesn't have a head injury. Coker thus is in the clear ahead of next Monday's game at Tampa Bay.

injuries.shortComment: Young completed 22 of 30 passes for 254 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 35-33 win over Baltimore.
injuries.longComment: The fourth-year QB posted his best single-game completion rate of the season (73.3 percent) while tossing multiple TDs for the third time in the last six contests, a stretch in which he's compiled a 9:5 TD:INT. Both of Young's scores came in the first half, as he connected with Mitchell Evans on a 23-yard TD and Tetairoa McMillan on a seven-yard strike. Young will look to keep rolling in Week 12 against Tampa Bay.

injuries.shortComment: Carlson caught two of his four targets for 30 yards during Chicago's win over the Lions on Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Carlson hadn't caught a pass across his previous three appearances this season but benefited from increased playing time after Colston Loveland (knee) exited the game in the first quarter. Carlson could continue to see increased usage if Loveland is forced to miss extended time.

injuries.shortComment: Raymond caught three of his five targets for 20 yards during Chicago's win over the Lions on Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Raymond had a solid outing against his former team, as he finished tied for fourth on the Bears in receptions. The 32-year-old has now caught 36 passes for 324 yards and a touchdown, in addition to racking up 209 punt-return yards across 11 games this season.

injuries.shortComment: Santos converted his only field-goal attempt and all four of his extra-point tries during Chicago's 39-35 win over the Detroit on Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Santos' lone field goal came from 40 yards out during the victory. The 35-year-old has converted 18 of his 22 field-goal attempts and 33 of his 34 extra-point tries across 11 games this season.

injuries.shortComment: Roush caught all five of his targets for 31 yards in Thursday's 39-35 win over the Lions.
injuries.longComment: Colston Loveland exited the game early with a knee injury, and as a result Roush wound up posting the best numbers of his brief career. The 2026 third-round pick hadn't caught more than two passes in a game prior to Thanksgiving, but with Cole Kmet (knee) already done for the season, a serious injury to Loveland would plant Roush at the top of the depth chart at tight end heading into a Week 13 clash with the Jaguars.

injuries.shortComment: Odunze caught six of nine targets for 87 yards and two touchdowns in Thursday's 39-35 win over the Lions.
injuries.longComment: The third-year wideout played hero in the fourth quarter on Thanksgiving. With the Bears down 35-24, Odunze hauled in a 41-yard strike from Caleb Williams (abdomen)  and then went up for a six-yard score in the back corner of the end zone with just three seconds left on the clock. Odunze sports a 42-660-3 line on 64 targets through 11 games, and if Colston Loveland (knee) ends up missing more time after exiting Thursday's game early, there could be more looks available for him in a Week 13 tilt against the Jaguars.

injuries.shortComment: Burden caught three of seven targets for 44 yards in Thursday's 39-35 win over the Lions.
injuries.longComment: The second-year wideout has taken a back seat to Rome Odunze coming out of Chicago's Week 10 bye. While Burden has managed just a 5-54-0 line on 10 targets over the last two games, Odunze topped those numbers on Thanksgiving alone with a 6-87-2 line on nine targets. Burden still has better overall numbers on the season, but the gap is closing rapidly. Colston Loveland (knee) left Thursday's game early, however, which could open up more volume for both of the Bears' top WRs. Burden will look to get rolling in Week 13 against the Jaguars.

injuries.shortComment: Monangai carried the ball eight times for 15 yards and two touchdowns and caught one of two targets for 14 yards in Thursday's 39-35 win over the Lions.
injuries.longComment: Once again Monangai took a back seat to D'Andre Swift in terms of volume, but he punched in rushing scores from one and two yards out. The junior member of the Bears' backfield is up to five TDs on the season in six games, all on the ground, and Monangai's goal-line role keeps him fantasy-relevant heading into a Week 13 clash with the Jaguars.

injuries.shortComment: Swift carried the ball nine times for 65 yards and a touchdown and caught seven of eight targets for 97 yards in Thursday's 39-35 win over the Lions.
injuries.longComment: While Kyle Monangai swooped in to score two TDs at the goal line, Swift put up impressive numbers of his own, leading the Bears in both rushing and receiving yards while hitting paydirt on a 30-yard run in the third quarter. The seven grabs and 97 receiving yards were both season highs for Swift, and the added volume came as a result of Colston Loveland's early exit due to a knee injury. If Loveland ends up missing more time, Swift's usage as a pass catcher could get a boost again in Week 13 against the Jaguars. He's already been plenty busy on that front this season, and through 11 contests he's compiled 959 scrimmage yards and a career-high 12 total TDs (10 rushing, two receiving).

injuries.shortComment: Williams said after Thursday's 39-35 win in Detroit that he's "fine" and likely just has "a bruise on his abdomen," Jason Lieser of the Chicago Sun-Times reports.
injuries.longComment: Williams seemingly went for a precautionary X-ray after Week 12 action due to a "weird fall" that occurred during Thursday's contest in which he engineered two TD drives in the final 8:20 of the fourth quarter to eke out a four-point victory. He completed 30 of 44 passes for 345 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions and recorded three carries for 15 yards. With plenty of time to recover before the Bears' next game Sunday, Dec. 6 against the Jaguars, Williams has a decent chance to avoid practice restrictions next week.

injuries.shortComment: Loveland (knee) has been ruled out from returning to Thursday's game in Detroit.
injuries.longComment: After Loveland was rolled up on in the middle of the first quarter, he was favoring his left knee as made his way to the sideline, where he visited the sideline tent before being carted to the locker room. Now that he officially won't return to this Week 12 contest, rookie third-round pick Sam Roush and veteran Stephen Carlson are the team's healthy and available tight ends.

injuries.shortComment: Jackson (elbow) is active for Thursday's Thanksgiving Day matchup versus the Lions.
injuries.longComment: Jackson dealt with an elbow issue through the short week of prep, but he's going to suit up Thursday. After playing a significant role on defense early in the campaign, the veteran linebacker has logged all but one of his snaps on special teams over Chicago's past three games, and that will likely continue to be his role against Detroit.

injuries.shortComment: Stevenson (groin) is active to face Detroit on Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Stevenson was a late addition to the injury report Wednesday as a limited practice participant due to a groin issue. However, he'll be able to push through the injury and suit up against Detroit. That's significant for the Bears, as Stevenson is tied for second on the team with five defensed passes this season.

injuries.shortComment: Keenum (coach's decision) is inactive and tabbed as the Bears' emergency third quarterback Thursday in Detroit.
injuries.longComment: Keenum will fill the Bears' emergency quarterback role for a sixth consecutive week. He'll be able to enter Thursday's contest only if both Caleb Williams and Tyson Bagent have to exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

injuries.shortComment: Gordon (shoulder) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Lions.
injuries.longComment: The cornerback didn't practice at all this week and will miss a second straight game after he was injured in Week 9 against the Bucs. Clark Phillips handled third cornerback duties in last Sunday's win over the Saints.

injuries.shortComment: Ahmed was elevated from the practice squad to the Bears' active roster Wednesday, Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune reports.
injuries.longComment: Roschon Johnson (ankle) was ruled out for Thursday's game, leaving the Bears with only two healthy options in the backfield going into Thanksgiving. With that, Ahmed will be up from the practice squad for the divisional tilt against the Lions.

injuries.shortComment: Johnson (ankle) has been ruled out  for Thursday's game against the Lions.
injuries.longComment: Johnson injured his ankle in Sunday's win over the Saints, and with the quick turnaround for Week 12, he won't be available against the Lions. The Bears will roll with D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai as their only healthy backs for Thursday's game.

injuries.shortComment: Lewis recorded seven tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints.
injuries.longComment: Playing in his 85th career regular-season game, Lewis' first-quarter sack of Tyler Shough on third-and-11 was the first of the safety's career. Lewis has started eight of the nine games in which he's appeared this season, logging 42 tackles (30 solo) and two pass breakups, including an interception.

injuries.shortComment: Thieneman recorded seven tackles (three solo) and an interception in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints.
injuries.longComment: Thieneman picked off Tyler Shough in New Orleans' territory in the second quarter, and the Bears turned it into a touchdown three plays later to go up 16-0. It was Thieneman's second interception of the season. The rookie safety is up to 64 tackles (34 solo), including 1.5 sacks, and six pass breakups across 10 games.

injuries.shortComment: Simmons recorded four tackles (three solo), including 3.0 sacks, in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints.
injuries.longComment: Picked up from the Titans ahead of the trade deadline, Simmons has been everything the Bears could've imagined and then some in three games with his new team. He's up to 14 tackles (nine solo), including 5.0 sacks, and a pair of pass breakups since joining Chicago.

injuries.shortComment: Thomas brought in two of three targets for 56 yards and added a 30-yard carry during the Bears' 21-13 win over the Saints on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Thomas was cleared to play Sunday after working through an ankle issue that prevented him from practicing Friday. The ankle didn't appear to bother him, as he turned his first touch of the game into a 30-yard rush midway through the second quarter before connecting with Caleb Williams for 40 and 16 yards in the third and fourth quarters, respectively. It was the rookie third-round wideout's best performance of the season, and while Chicago boasts talented pass catchers like Luther Burden, Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland, Thomas' big-play potential could be something that the Bears lean into for Thanksgiving Day against the Lions, whose defense ranks 27th in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (233.1) and 29th in passing touchdowns allowed (21).

injuries.shortComment: Dugger (quadriceps) was not listed on the Bengals' injury report Wednesday.
injuries.longComment: Dugger has apparently overcome his quadriceps injury after being declared inactive for Monday night's loss to the Commanders. The reserve safety is set to practice in full capacity through Week 12 prep ahead of Sunday's game against the Saints.

injuries.shortComment: Risner (knee) is considered day-to-day, Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com reported Wednesday.
injuries.longComment: Risner did not play in the Bengals' loss to the Commanders on Monday night due to multiple knee injuries. The starting right guard remains day-to-day with the issue, meaning he could return for Sunday's game against the Saints. If Risner cannot suit up for Week 12, Jalen Rivers is set to start at right guard again.

injuries.shortComment: Endries caught four of five targets for 33 yards during Monday night's 22-20 loss to the Commanders.
injuries.longComment: Endries reeled in a career-high four passes while playing 15 snaps on offense in Week 11. The rookie is still behind Mike Gesicki and Drew Sample in the pecking order at tight end ahead of Week 12 versus the Saints.

injuries.shortComment: Young caught one of two targets for a four-yard touchdown during Monday night's 22-20 loss to the Commanders.
injuries.longComment: Young reeled in his first pass since Week 3, and he notched his first career touchdown in the process. The wide receiver connected with quarterback Joe Burrow for a four-yard score in the third quarter, momentarily providing Cincinnati with a 17-10 lead. Young's 22 offensive snaps ranked third at his position behind Ja'Marr Chase (56) and Tee Higgins (56) while ahead of Dohnte Meyers (21), but Young may revert to a smaller role on offense with Andrei Iosivas (thumb) on track to return in Week 12.

injuries.shortComment: Sample caught his lone target for nine yards during the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday.
injuries.longComment: After catching a touchdown pass from Joe Burrow in Week 10 against the Steelers, Sample saw only one target from the superstar quarterback during Monday's loss. Sample has caught one pass or zero in seven of 10 regular-season games and has an 11-72-2 receiving line on 12 targets while operating as the Bengals' TE2 behind Mike Gesicki.

injuries.shortComment: McPherson made both of his field-goal attempts and went 2-for-2 on extra-point tries during the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday.
injuries.longComment: After both teams went scoreless in a rainy first quarter, McPherson put the Bengals on the board with a 38-yard field goal in the second. He nailed a 56-yarder late in the fourth to give the Bengals a 20-19 lead, but his would-be game winner didn't come to pass as the Commanders raced down the field to set up Drew Stevens for a 26-yard field goal to seal the win for Washington. McPherson has made only five field goals (on six attempts) over the Bengals' last five games, but his 35 point-afters are second-most in the NFL behind Eddy Pineiro (36). The Bengals will head back home for Week 12 against the Saints, whose defense ranks 23rd in the NFL in points allowed per game (25.7).

injuries.shortComment: Meyers caught one of two passes for two yards, returned six kickoffs for 150 yards and returned one punt for five yards during the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday.
injuries.longComment: Most of Meyers' production came on special teams as a returner, and his one catch was his fewest since Week 7 against the Ravens, when he failed to record a reception. He's caught two passes or fewer in seven of 10 regular-season games, and his minimal role on offense would shrink even more once Andrei Iosivas (thumb) is cleared to return from injured reserve. The Bengals will head home for Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Perine turned six carries into 26 yards and caught all four of his targets for 71 yards during the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday.
injuries.longComment: The Commanders' defense focused its attention toward slowing down both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. That opened up the field for Perine, with most of his production coming on a 44-yard catch late in the second quarter, and the drive ended two plays later with a 31-yard touchdown pass from Joe Burrow to Higgins. Perine finished second on the Bengals in both catches and receiving yards behind tight end Mike Gesicki, and the RB's 26 rushing yards were well ahead of Chase Brown's six. Perine has at least 10 touches in each of his last three games, but Cincinnati's offense is mustering only 79.4 rushing yards per game, which is third-worst in the NFL. Given Brown's struggles this season, Perine could take on a larger role in the backfield for Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Gesicki brought in five of six targets for 77 yards in the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday night.
injuries.longComment: The veteran tight end finished with a team-high yardage total while coming just a yard short of equaling his best tally of the season as well. Gesicki's biggest catch came late in the fourth quarter on the Bengals' final drive, when he hauled in a 32-yard pass from Joe Burrow over the middle to get the Bengals down to  the Commanders' 33-yard line. Gesicki's production continues to have some game-to-game volatility, but he'll draw another favorable matchup in a Week 12 home clash with the Saints on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Brown rushed six times for six yards and brought in five of eight targets for 30 yards in the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday night.
injuries.longComment: As his final line indicates, Brown was completely stonewalled by a talented Commanders run defense, although backfield mate Samaje Perine, who equaled Brown's carry total, was able to average 4.3 yards per tote with his opportunities and  added 71 receiving yards. Brown did find a way to make his usual impact as a receiver, tying for the team lead in receptions and finishing second in targets to Ja'Marr Chase. Brown's carry and rushing yardage totals were both season lows, but he should have appreciably better conditions for production on the ground in a Week 12 home matchup against the Saints on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Higgins brought in two of three targets for 43 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday night.
injuries.longComment: Although Joe Burrow threw for 300 yards, both Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase found tough sledding against a Commanders secondary geared up to stop them. Higgins did salvage his fantasy night with his seventh touchdown catch of the season on a picturesque over-the-shoulder 31-yard grab down the left sideline on the first play after the two-minute warning in the first half. Higgins has six of his scoring receptions in the last five games heading into a favorable Week 12 home matchup against the Saints on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Chase secured five of nine targets for 31 yards in the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday night.
injuries.longComment: The Commanders focused on keeping Chase in check after his 231-yard outburst against the Steelers in Week 10, and they executed that plan to near perfection. The superstar wideout finished with his third-lowest yardage total of the season, and his sparsest since Week 4. Chase still extended his streak of five-plus-catch efforts to six games, and he'll look to bounce back to his usual level of production in a Week 12 home matchup against a vulnerable Saints defense Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Burrow completed 28 of 40 passes for 300 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed twice for minus-1 yard in the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday night.
injuries.longComment: The Bengals offense started slowly and was shut out altogether in the first quarter, but Burrow was able to lead his team to 10 second-quarter points partly via a 31-yard touchdown pass to Tee Higgins. The prolific signal-caller added a four-yard scoring toss to Colbie Young in the third quarter, and Burrow then helped lead Cincinnati downfield for a go-ahead Evan McPherson 56-yard field goal with 46 seconds remaining, albeit after narrowly avoiding an interception and then taking a third-down sack. Nevertheless, the Bengals came up short when Jayden Daniels led the Commanders on a five-play, 64-yard game-winning march, but Burrow finished with his fourth tally of at least 300 passing yards this season. He'll look to put his team back in the win column in a favorable Week 12 home matchup against the Saints on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Cook (ankle) has returned to Monday night's matchup with the Commanders, Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com reports.
injuries.longComment: The safety suffered a right ankle injury late in the first half and was questionable to return. Now that he's back, he should be able to resume his role in the lineup at free safety.

injuries.shortComment: The Bengals reinstated Parker from injured reserve and list him as active for Monday's game against the Commanders.
injuries.longComment: Parker had been on IR all season due to a knee injury but was added back to the 53-man roster after turning in five consecutive full practices upon having his 21-day evaluation window opened Nov. 12. He'll serve as a depth option at guard during Monday's contest.

injuries.shortComment: The Bengals reinstated Bozeman (forearm) from injured reserve and list him as active  for Monday's game against the Commanders.
injuries.longComment: Bozeman was designated for return from IR on Thursday and needed just three full practices before the Bengals were comfortable adding him back to the 53-man roster. While serving mainly as a special-teams contributor, Bozeman tallied four tackles through the first five weeks of the season before landing on IR due to a broken forearm.

injuries.shortComment: Hill (illness) is active for Monday night's contest against the Commanders.
injuries.longComment: Hill was absent from practice for the entire week due to an illness, but he is now good to go for Monday Night Football. The 26-year-old will operate in his starting role at slot cornerback versus Washington.

injuries.shortComment: Davis (hamstring) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Commanders, Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Davis strung together multiple full practices since being designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 12, but he still drew the doubtful tag for Monday's game. He'll end up missing a seventh consecutive game due to a hamstring injury, and his next chance to return is Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Iosivas (thumb) was downgraded to out for Monday's game against the Commanders, Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Iosivas will remain on injured reserve for at least one more week, after the Bengals had listed him as doubtful heading into Monday's contest following a trio of full practices from Thursday through Saturday. If the fourth-year wideout can turn in another full slate of practices in Week 12, he should have a better chance of being restored to the 53-man roster ahead of the Bengals' Nov. 29 matchup with the Saints.

injuries.shortComment: The Bengals placed Burks (groin) on injured reserve Saturday.
injuries.longComment: Burks has been working through a groin issue for the past couple of weeks, and he aggravated the injury during the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday. His placement on IR means he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, so his next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Panthers on Sunday, Dec. 20.

injuries.shortComment: Flacco took the field for the Bengals' final possession of Sunday's 38-18 win over the Steelers, attempting no passes while handing off to running back Tahj Brooks on all three of his snaps.
injuries.longComment: With the Bengals having built their lead to 20 by the midway point of the fourth quarter, head coach Zac Taylor pulled starter Joe Burrow from the contest and turned to Flacco to run down the clock in the win. The appearance was Flacco's third of the season, but the veteran signal-caller still has yet to attempt a pass.

injuries.shortComment: Whiteheart was listed as full participant in Cleveland's practice estimate Thursday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Whiteheart popped up on the injury report Wednesday due to a hip issue but should be good to go for Sunday's matchup versus the Raiders. The 26-year-old tight end has caught four of his seven targets for 48 yards and a touchdown across 10 games this season.

injuries.shortComment: Boston (quadriceps) was listed as a non-participant on Thursday's practice estimate, Sam Warren of The Athleticreports.
injuries.longComment: The Browns didn't actually practice Thursday, but Boston's estimated 'DNP' on the heels of Wednesday's missed session puts the focus on what the starting wideout is able to Friday ahead of the team posting its final injury report for Sunday night's 8:20 p.m. ET game against the Raiders. If Boston isn't cleared for the contest prior to the weekend, his fantasy managers will be put in a tricky spot, considering Cleveland's late Week 12 kickoff.

injuries.shortComment: Fannin (groin) was listed as a full practice participant on Thursday's injury report, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: The Browns didn't hold a practice on Thanksgiving Day, but the fact that Fannin was estimated as a full participant Thursday indicates that the second-year tight end is on track to play against the Raiders on Sunday. Fannin has caught at least six passes in three of his last four outings, and has compiled a 25-378-1 receiving line on 32 targets over that span.

injuries.shortComment: Williams (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Williams may have picked up the injury during the Browns' Week 10 win over the Texans, when he logged nine tackles (five solo) and one pass defense. The injury designation follows the Browns' Week 11 bye, and he'll have two more chances to increase his practice participation ahead of Sunday's game against Las Vegas.

injuries.shortComment: McGuire (calf) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: The Browns are coming out of a bye, so it's unclear whether McGuire picked up the injury during the Browns' Week 10 win over the Texans. Regardless, he'll have two more opportunities to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders.

injuries.shortComment: Hickman (concussion) logged a full practice Wednesday, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Hickman was held out of the Browns' Week 10 win over the Texans while in the league's concussion protocol. Cleveland's Week 11 bye gave him extra time to recover, and while his full session Wednesday is encouraging, Hickman would need to pass an evaluation by an independent neurologist in order to clear protocol and be available to play Sunday against Las Vegas.

injuries.shortComment: Sanders (hip) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Sanders was designated to return from injured reserve Tuesday, and he was limited in his first practice session since suffering a hip injury against the Jets in Week 5. He'll have two more opportunities to log a full practice, but Sanders would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Raiders.

injuries.longComment: questionable
