injuries.shortComment: Okuayinonu (foot) was spotted walking without a limp in the 49ers' locker room Wednesday, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Okuayinonu suffered a broken foot in practice ahead of Week 1 and required surgery. He appears to be making progress and could return at some point before the end of the regular season. The 28-year-old appeared in 15 regular-season games last season, and made 12 starts and recorded 23 tackles (16 solo), including 3.0 sacks, and a forced fumble.

injuries.shortComment: The 49ers activated Hobbs (groin) from injured reserve Wednesday.
injuries.longComment: San Francisco needed to make a decision on Hobbs after his 21-day practice window was set to close. The veteran cornerback will be looking to make his 2026 debut Sunday against the Seahawks.

injuries.shortComment: San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan said Wednesday that Stribling (ankle) is likely at least "a couple weeks away" from returning to practice, Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle reports. "I don't know. I mean, nothing's changed," Shanahan said, regarding a timeline for the rookie receiver.
injuries.longComment: Stribling was diagnosed with a deltoid sprain of his left ankle after getting injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams in Australia and underwent surgery Sept. 16. The 23-year-old was handed an estimated recovery timeline of about 10 weeks, leaving the 49ers optimistic that he would be ready to play at some point in December. While Shanahan indicated that Stribling's timeline doesn't appear to have changed, the young wideout will need to get back on the practice field before the 49ers can hone in on a more precise target date for him to resume playing. Given the haziness of his return date along with the fact that he could face limitations with his snaps once activated, Stribling likely isn't worth holding in redraft leagues at this point in the season.

injuries.shortComment: Willis went without a target while logging nine snaps on offense and 21 on special teams in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Vikings in Mexico City.
injuries.longComment: Willis has suited up in each of the 49ers' last nine games but has received little run on offense while the team's top two tight ends -- George Kittle and Luke Farrell -- have remained healthy throughout the season. The 27-year-old has logged single-digit snaps on offense in five straight contests and has yet to draw a target in 2026.

injuries.shortComment: Farrell turned his lone target into a seven-yard reception in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Vikings in Mexico City.
injuries.longComment: Farrell has suited up in each of the 49ers' first 10 games, but despite logging double-digit snaps in each contest, he's produced just four catches for 40 yards on seven targets. He'll continue to serve mainly as a blocking tight end on offense while also serving as a key contributor on the 49ers' special-teams units.

injuries.shortComment: Brown recorded four tackles (three solo) and a pick-six during the 49ers' 35-10 win over the Vikings on Sunday in Mexico City.
injuries.longComment: Brown picked off a pass from Kirk Cousins intended for Tai Felton late in the second quarter, which Brown returned 18 yards to the house to extend the 49ers' lead to 28-10. It was his first interception of 2026 and sixth of his career, and Brown is up to 55 tackles (31 solo) and four pass defenses through 10 regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Warner recorded eight tackles (four solo) and a pass breakup in Sunday night's 35-10 win over the Vikings.
injuries.longComment: The four-time First-Team All-Pro linebacker has double-digit tackles in five of 10 games this season and is up to 96 tackles (42 solo), including 0.5 sacks, five forced fumbles, four pass breakups and a fumble recovery on 96 percent of the Niners' defensive snaps.

injuries.shortComment: Cowing returned one punt for no gain during San Francisco's win over the Vikings on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Cowing saw limited action in the win, playing just six snaps on offense and two on special teams. The 25-year-old hasn't been targeted across the last two games and should continue to serve a depth role with Mike Evans now healthy.

injuries.shortComment: James rushed twice for seven yards during Sunday night's 35-10 win over the Vikings.
injuries.longComment: James went without a touch on offense for the majority of the game, but he was able to turn the team's final two carries of the game into seven yards late in the fourth quarter. The running back was on the field for five offensive plays, and he'll remain the team's No. 3 option behind Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black in Week 12 against the Seahawks.

injuries.shortComment: Juszczyk caught both of his targets for 13 yards during Sunday night's 35-10 win over the Vikings.
injuries.longComment: Juszczyk was able to reel in his first two passes since Week 7, notching his fourth multi-catch performance of the year. The fullback has now caught 10 of 13 targets for 89 yards and two touchdowns while also adding a four-yard rush over nine contests to open the 2026 season.

injuries.shortComment: Pineiro made all five of his PATs in Sunday night's 35-10 win over the Vikings.
injuries.longComment: It was the veteran kicker's third game this season that he didn't attempt a field goal, but he's now gone three straight games with exactly five extra points. Pineiro now leads the league in both point-after attempts (40) and makes (36), but he's attempted just 11 field goals in a highly efficient San Francisco offense. The lack of field goals certainly keeps him from being a top fantasy kicker.

injuries.shortComment: Allen totaled three catches (on four targets) for 38 yards during Sunday's 35-10 victory against the Vikings in Mexico City.
injuries.longComment: Sunday marked Allen's first time working with Mike Evans, the 49ers' top wide receiver, and the latter dominated the attention of QB Brock Purdy, posting a 6-109-1 line on seven targets in his first game action since Week 6. If Evans' Achilles issue flares up at any point, Allen may be thrust into WR1 duties, which could yield more consistent results as he becomes more acclimated to head coach Kyle Shanahan's offense. For now, though, Allen will play a distant second to Evans for as long as the latter is healthy and available.

injuries.shortComment: Bradford (knee) was estimated as a limited participant in Seattle's practice estimate Thursday, Bob Condotta of The Seattle Times reports.
injuries.longComment: Bradford was listed as limited for the second consecutive day as he continues to deal with a knee injury. The 2023 fourth-round pick should continue to serve as the team's backup right guard behind Grey Zabel during Sunday's matchup against the 49ers.

injuries.shortComment: Cross (ankle) was listed as a full participant in Seattle's practice estimate Thursday, Bob Condotta of The Seattle Times reports.
injuries.longComment: Cross is seemingly healthy again after having missed the team's last three games due to an ankle injury. The 2022 first-round pick should resume his role as Seattle's starting left tackle during Sunday's matchup against the 49ers.

injuries.shortComment: Lock (elbow) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Bob Condotta of The Seattle Times reports.
injuries.longComment: Lock has been working through an elbow issue to his throwing arm since late October, which has limited his participation in the first two practices of Week 12 prep. He started in each of the Seahawks' two games prior to the Week 11 bye, but is expected to revert to backup duties provided Sam Darnold (quadriceps) is cleared to start against the 49ers on Sunday. If Lock isn't available to play against San Francisco, then Jalen Milroe (illness) would be in line to operate as Seattle's QB2 behind Darnold.

injuries.shortComment: questionable
injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: questionable
injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: Smith-Njigba (ankle) was listed as limited on Thursday's injury report, Bob Condotta of The Seattle Times reports.
injuries.longComment: An ankle injury has left Smith-Njigba listed as limited on both of the Seahawks' Week 12 practice reports so far, meaning he has just one more chance to get back to full Friday, at which point the Seahawks may tag him with a designation for Sunday's game at San Francisco. Through 10 contests this season, he's failed to reach the century mark in receiving yards just two times and also has 10 touchdown catches.

injuries.shortComment: Jones (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: It is unclear where Jones picked up his knee injury, but it still appears to be bothering the linebacker after the Seahawks' Week 11 bye. Jones will have Thursday and Friday's practice sessions to upgrade to full participation and avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's divisional contest against the 49ers.

injuries.shortComment: Head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters Wednesday that Nelson (knee) will not play against the 49ers on Sunday, Brady Henderson of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Nelson underwent a minor procedure on his knee in early November and will be sidelined for a second consecutive game. He's had additional time to rest thanks to the Seahawks' Week 11 bye, and Macdonald relayed Wednesday that the team is "hopeful" that Nelson will be cleared to return for Week 13 against the Cowboys on Monday, Dec. 7. Greg Zabel will likely start at left guard in Nelson's absence.

injuries.shortComment: Lucas (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Brady Henderson of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Per John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site, head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters Wednesday that Lucas is not a candidate for injured reserve but is expected to miss "days to weeks" due to an ankle sprain that he suffered in Week 10 against the Raiders. Josh Jones, Bobby Hart and Chase Lundt are all candidates to start at right tackle for as long as Lucas is sidelined.

injuries.shortComment: questionable
injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: questionable
injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: Darnold (quadriceps) practiced fully Wednesday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Head coach Mike Macdonald told Brady Henderson of ESPN.com on Wednesday that Darnold will start Sunday at San Francisco if he fares well in practice this week, and a full practice is a good place for the quarterback to kick things off. Darnold has missed the last two contests due to a quad injury and cracked ribs, but only the first concern was mentioned on Wednesday's practice report, indicating his improved level of health.

injuries.shortComment: questionable
injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: The Seahawks placed Holani (knee) on injured reserve Monday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Holani was knocked out of the Seahawks' last game in Week 10 at Las Vegas due to a knee injury that eventually was deemed to be an MCL sprain. Per Brady Henderson of ESPN.com, head coach Mike Macdonald said he was uncertain if Holani will require surgery, but the running back will be sidelined for at least four games by virtue of landing on IR. In the meantime, Emanuel Wilson will serve as the team's No. 3 back behind Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price.

injuries.shortComment: Witherspoon logged four solo tackles, including 2.0 sacks, in the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Coach Mike MacDonald dialed up the blitz against rookie first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza in his first career start. Two of Witherspoon's four tackles in the Seahawks' win came behind the line of scrimmage off cornerback blitzes against Mendoza. Witherspoon also played all 59 of the team's defensive snaps in the one-score win.

injuries.shortComment: Myers missed his sole field-goal attempt and made three PATs in the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Myers missed a 44-yard field-goal attempt with 7:05 remaining in the game that would have put the Seahawks up 14 points. The kicker is now 16-for-19 on field-goal attempts and 21-for-23 on PATs over 10 regular-season contests in 2026.

injuries.shortComment: Kupp hauled in his lone target for a 34-yard touchdown during the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: It was the third time this season that Kupp recorded only one catch, but the veteran wide receiver made his lone reception count when he found open space on a broken play to connect with Drew Lock for a TD late in the first quarter. It was the third touchdown catch of the season for Kupp, two of which have come over his last three outings. He'll enter the bye with a 23-272-3 line on 35 targets through 10 regular-season games, and the Seahawks' next matchup will take place in Week 12 on the road against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

injuries.shortComment: Horton failed to garner a target during Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders.
injuries.longComment: Horton failed to reel in a pass for the first time since Week 7, and his 10 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Seattle behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (43), Cooper Kupp (35) and Rashid Shaheed (25). Horton will continue to be an unappealing fantasy option as long as he's buried below the other three wideouts on the depth chart.

injuries.shortComment: Barner caught all three targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders.
injuries.longComment: Barner has been held below 25 receiving yards in eight of 10 games this season and has more rushing touchdowns (two) than receiving scores (one) during the 2026 campaign. He's the definition of a low-floor, touchdown-or-bust fantasy option headed into the team's bye week.

injuries.shortComment: Shaheed caught one pass for eight yards on two targets in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders.
injuries.longComment: After missing the previous two games with a knee injury, Shaheed returned against Las Vegas and maintained his role as the WR3 for Seattle. He played 25 of 57 offensive snaps and remained a non-factor in the box score. Shaheed has yet to hit 70 receiving yards in a game this season and has zero touchdowns as a pass catcher. He's off the fantasy radar.

injuries.shortComment: Price posted nine carries for 36 yards and one touchdown and gathered in his only target for eight yards during Sunday's 21-13 victory at Las Vegas.
injuries.longComment: This marks Price's fewest touches in a game since returning from IR in Week 8, and he actually was doubled up in the category by position mate Zach Charbonnet, who turned his 20 rushes into 94 yards. Having said that, Price salvaged his day with a 12-yard TD, the first of his career, on the ground in the third quarter. The breakdown of work between the two may signal what's to come in the Seahawks backfield after the team's Week 11 bye, with Price and company set to face off with the NFC West-leading 49ers on the road on Sunday, Nov. 29.

injuries.shortComment: Charbonnet churned out 94 yards on 20 carries during Sunday's 21-13 win in Las Vegas.
injuries.longComment: Charbonnet was eased in to the mix in Weeks 8 and 9, going from nine touches in the first contest to 17 in the latter. This time around, though, he doubled up fellow RB Jadarian Price in touches (10) and more than did so in terms from yards from scrimmage (44). It may signal that Charbonnet is the Seahawks' clear-cut No. 1 backfield option moving forward, but he won't have a chance to prove as much until after the team's Week 11 bye on Sunday, Nov. 29, at San Francisco.

injuries.shortComment: Reed is doubtful to return to Sunday's game against Las Vegas due to a toe injury.
injuries.longComment: Reed limped off the field during the first half and was subsequently deemed doubtful to return. Brandon Pili should get a lot more defensive snaps in the likely scenario that Reed is unable to re-enter Sunday's contest.

injuries.shortComment: Parrish (back) was listed a limited participant in Tampa Bay's practice estimate Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Parrish is still dealing with the back injury that he suffered in the Week 11 loss to the Lions. The 22-year-old will likely need to be upgraded to a full participant by Saturday's practice to avoid carrying an injury designation into Monday's matchup against the Panthers.

injuries.shortComment: Winfield (ankle) was listed a non-participant in Tampa Bay's practice estimate Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Winfield is still dealing with the ankle injury that he suffered during the Week 9 loss to the Bears. If he is unable to participate at some point over the next two days of practice, the 2020 second-round pick could be in danger of missing a second consecutive game

injuries.shortComment: Trotter (oblique) was listed as a limited participant in Tampa Bay's practice estimate Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Trotter popped up on the injury report Thursday, casting doubt on his availability for Monday's matchup against the Panthers. If the rookie second-round pick ends up being unable to play, SirVocea Dennis would likely start at inside linebacker alongside Alex Anzalone.

injuries.shortComment: McMillan (knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
injuries.longComment: McMillan has missed the Buccaneers' last seven games while recovering from an MCL sprain in his left knee that he sustained against the Vikings in Week 3. He was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday, and even if he practices in full over the next two days, he would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Monday's game against the Panthers.

injuries.shortComment: The Buccaneers opened the 21-day practice window for Rozeboom (finger) on Wednesday, Scott Smith of the team's official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Rozeboom has been on injured reserve for the Buccaneers' last four games while recovering from a finger injury that he sustained in late October. Tampa Bay's first practice of Week 12 prep is Thursday, so Rozeboom's participation over those three sessions will determine whether he's recovered enough to be activated from IR ahead of Monday's game against the Panthers.

injuries.shortComment: Kieft played all 12 of his snaps on special teams in Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.
injuries.longComment: Kieft has played just 11 total snaps on offense over his nine appearances with Tampa Bay this season while Cade Otton, Payne Durham and Bauer Sharp have been prioritized ahead of him at tight end. On the rare occasions he takes the field with the offense, Kieft typically handles a blocking role. He hasn't drawn a target in any game since his second season in the NFL in 2023.

injuries.shortComment: Sharp went without a target while logging 12 of the Buccaneers' 69 offensive snaps in Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.
injuries.longComment: Sharp's 17 percent offensive snap share placed him third among Tampa Bay tight ends, and he trails Cade Otton (97 percent) and Payne Durham (22 percent). The rookie sixth-round pick out of LSU has rarely seen involvement in the passing game over his limited playing time on offense this season, recording a 21-yard reception on two targets over 10 appearances.

injuries.shortComment: Durham wasn't targeted while playing 15 of the Buccaneers' 69 snaps on offense and 15 on special teams in Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.
injuries.longComment: Durham's lone contribution in the box score came on the Buccaneers' first play of the day, when he recovered a fumble by quarterback Baker Mayfield. Though he's suited up for each of the Buccaneers' 10 games and has logged double-digit snaps on offense in the past six contests, Durham has recorded just one reception (for five yards) on two targets throughout the season. He's been deployed mainly as a blocking tight end, running routes on just 22 plays on the campaign.

injuries.shortComment: Smith logged nine tackles (six solo) during Tampa Bay's loss to the Lions on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Smith finished second on the team in tackles behind Josiah Trotter, who had 14 (eight solo). Smith has now compiled seven or more tackles across four of his last five appearances and will look to maintain this level of production during the Week 12 matchup against the Panthers.

injuries.shortComment: Johnson caught two of three targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.
injuries.longComment: After being benched in the Bucs' pre-Week 9 bye loss to the Bears, Ted Hurst was back in the good graces of the coaching staff and played ahead of Johnson as the WR3 behind Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin. That left Johnson as the fourth receiver, playing just 20 of 69 offensive snaps. He has 13 catches for 271 yards and one touchdown on 23 targets across 10 games this season.

injuries.shortComment: Simmons is in concussion protocol following Sunday's loss to the Lions, Brianna Dix of the Buccaneers' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Simmons played 17 defensive snaps in Sunday's loss but did not appear in the box score. The defensive tackle has now entered the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will need to be cleared by an independent neurologist to return to full-contact football activities.

injuries.shortComment: Morrison (hamstring) underwent an MRI on Monday, Brianna Dix of the Buccaneers' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Both Morrison and Jacob Parrish (back) were injured in Sunday's loss to Detroit, forcing Tampa Bay to dip into its cornerback depth. Kevin Knowles picked up the extra snaps opposing Zyon McCollum, with Keionte Scott covering the slot.

injuries.shortComment: McLaughlin made all three of his extra-point attempts in Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.
injuries.longComment: After making multiple field goals in four straight games leading up to Sunday's game, McLaughlin didn't attempt a field goal for just the second time this season. The veteran kicker remains perfect on 43 kicks this season, going 22-for-22 on field goals and 21-for-21 on PATs. He's a valuable fantasy kicker headed into next Monday night's home date with the Panthers.

injuries.shortComment: Tucker didn't record any stats during Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.
injuries.longComment: Tucker didn't garner any touches on offense for the third straight week as Tampa Bay opted to use Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell exclusively in the backfield. Tucker will continue to have little to no fantasy value as long as both Irving and Gainwell are available for the Buccaneers.

injuries.shortComment: Otton caught one pass for eight yards on three targets in Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.
injuries.longComment: The tight end earned just a 9.1 percent target share and continues to be nearly invisible in the box score despite being an every-down player who runs virtually every pass route for the Bucs. Otton has just one touchdown since Week 11 of the 2024 season and has just one career 100-yard receiving game across 73 regular-season contests. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet who clearly busts far more than he hits.

injuries.shortComment: Godwin caught three passes for 18 yards on three targets in Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.
injuries.longComment: The veteran wideout ran a team-high 41 routes on Baker Mayfield's 44 dropbacks, but Godwin continues to produce very little with his immense playing time. He's been held under 40 receiving yards in eight straight games and has yet to have a 50-yard receiving game this season. Godwin also has zero touchdowns. He's a low-floor, low-ceiling fantasy option headed into next Monday night's date with the Panthers.

injuries.shortComment: Hurst caught five of seven targets for 56 yards and two touchdowns during Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.
injuries.longComment: Hurst led the team in targets, and his five catches and 56 receiving yards were new season highs. The wide receiver was able to reach paydirt twice, reeling in a 23-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Baker Mayfield in the second quarter before the pair connected for a four-yard score in the fourth quarter. Hurst has now caught 16 of 32 targets for 224 yards and three touchdowns over 10 contests this season.

injuries.shortComment: Gainwell rushed four times for 16 yards and brought in four of five targets for 43 yards in the Buccaneers 31-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Gainwell held his usual complementary role on the ground behind a busy Bucky Irving, yet with the Buccaneers trailing throughout the second half, Gainwell was able to finish second in receptions, receiving yards and targets on the day for Tampa Bay. The veteran back has back-to-back 16-yard efforts on the ground, but Gainwell has a combined 7-103-0 line through the air in that same span heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Panthers on Monday night, Nov. 30.

injuries.shortComment: Egbuka brought in two of five targets for 18 yards in the Buccaneers' 31-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Egbuka couldn't do much despite tying for the second-most targets on the afternoon for the Buccaneers. The 2025 first-round pick's catch total tied his season low, and he also posted his third sub-20-yard tally of the season. Egbuka has now been held under 50 receiving yards in five consecutive contests heading into a Week 12 Monday night home showdown against the Panthers on Nov. 30.

injuries.shortComment: Mayfield completed 20 of 33 passes for 187 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed six times for 36 yards in the Buccaneers' 31-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday. He also committed a fumble that stayed with Tampa Bay.
injuries.longComment: Mayfield fought through foot and thumb injuries to take the field in a critical game for the 3-6 Buccaneers, but he wasn't able to keep pace with Jared Goff and Jahmyr Gibbs. Mayfield did throw multiple touchdown passes for the first time this season, hitting rookie Ted Hurst for scoring strikes of 23 and four yards. Mayfield's rushing yardage total was also a new season high, and he'll next take aim at the Panthers' beatable secondary in a Week 12 divisional home matchup on Monday night, Nov. 30.

injuries.shortComment: Irving rushed 18 times for 68 yards and a touchdown and brought in three of four targets for 32 yards in the Buccaneers' 31-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Irving worked hard all afternoon against a feisty Lions defense, and outside of his game-long 23-yard run, he scuffled to 45 yards on 17 carries. Irving worked around a hard shot to the abdomen that he sustained in the second half, and he did manage to contribute a rushing touchdown for the fourth straight game when he went in from one yard out in the latter portion of the third quarter. Irving has now equaled a career high with eight rushing touchdowns, and he's 107 yards short of his second career 1,000-yard season on the ground heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Panthers on Monday night, Nov. 30.

injuries.shortComment: Franklin-Myers (back) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
injuries.longComment: Franklin-Myers' practice reps were limited Wednesday due to a lingering back issue, but his full session Thursday puts the veteran defensive lineman on track to play in Sunday's AFC South tilt against the Jaguars. Franklin-Myers is off to a disappointing start to his Titans tenure, with the 2018 fourth-rounder accumulating 18 tackles (seven solo), including 1.5 sacks, and one pass defense through 10 regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: questionable
injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: Flott (neck) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Turron Davenport of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Flott exited the Titans' Week 11 loss to the Jaguars early with a neck injury and did not return to the contest. The cornerback remains sidelined due to the recent injury, and it remains unclear how much time he is expected to miss. Flott will need to upgrade his practice participation by Friday to have any shot at playing in Sunday's divisional contest with the Jaguars.

injuries.shortComment: Adams (illness) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Turron Davenport of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Adams has recovered from the illness that sidelined him for the Titans' Week 11 loss to the Cowboys. The safety has already returned to full practice participation and should be all set to continue stringing together prep sessions in anticipation of Sunday's game against the Jaguars.

injuries.shortComment: Granson logged all 16 of his snaps on special teams in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.
injuries.longComment: Granson displayed some pass-catching ability in his first five seasons in the league between stops with the Colts and Eagles, but the Titans have deployed him almost exclusively on special teams in 2026. He's been active for just four of the team's first 10 contests and has drawn just one target while playing three total snaps on offense.

injuries.shortComment: Martin-Robinson played all but one of his 24 snaps on special teams in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.
injuries.longComment: The third-year tight end out of Temple is a core contributor on special teams but has been an afterthought on offense throughout the season. Martin-Robinson hasn't played double-digit snaps on offense in any of his nine appearances and has yet to draw a target.

injuries.shortComment: Winston recorded seven total tackles (four solo) during Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.
injuries.longComment: Winston was able to register at least seven stops for the sixth time this season while playing every defensive snap in Week 11. The safety has now compiled 63 total tackles (35 solo), a forced fumble and a fumble recovery over eight contests so far this season.

injuries.shortComment: Gray posted eight tackles (four solo) during the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Gray finished second on the Titans in tackles behind Joshua Williams (11) in a game that saw Tennessee's defense yield six consecutive touchdown drives to Dallas. Gray has recorded eight stops in back-to-back outings and is up to 54 tackles (30 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and two pass defenses (including one interception).

injuries.shortComment: Wiliams posted 11 tackles (nine solo) during the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: The Titans' defense failed to put up much of a fight against the Cowboys, who scored touchdowns on each of their first six offensive drives. Williams led Tennessee with a career-high 11 stops, and it was the first time he reached double-digits tackles in a game since entering the league as a fourth-round selection of the Chiefs in the 2022 NFL Draft. He's up to 33 tackles (22 solo) and two pass defenses across five regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Tennessee signed Thornton (fibula) off the Panthers' practice squad Tuesday, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Starting corner Cor'Dale Flott suffered a neck injury during Sunday's game at Dallas, which could be part of the reason the Titans are looking to add depth in their secondary. Over two games with the Panthers this season, Thornton recorded eight tackles (six solo) and an interception.

injuries.shortComment: Bellinger made one catch for five yards in the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Bellinger played 26 offensive snaps and five special-teams snaps in the contest. The tight end capitalized on his sole target but was primarily utilized as a blocker in the blowout loss.

injuries.shortComment: Restrepo caught his lone target for five yards in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.
injuries.longComment: Even with Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) out, Restrepo played as the Titans' WR5 against Dallas, as his 17 offensive snaps trailed all four of Carnell Tate (61), Chimere Dike (53), Elic Ayomanor (36) and Calvin Ridley (26). Restrepo played 11 of his 13 snaps in the slot, where Robinson operated prior to his injury, but it was actually Dike and Daniel Bellinger who saw the biggest boosts in slot rate with Robinson out.

injuries.shortComment: Carter reverted to the Titans' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
injuries.longComment: With Tyjae Spears (knee) back on the shelf and sent to injured reserve over the weekend, Carter played 14 of 68 offensive snaps behind Tony Pollard in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys. Carter ended up carrying the ball four times for nine yards and caught his lone target for two yards. He should remain Pollard's backup for at least the next three games while Spears is out, unless the Titans have a change of heart and want to start getting rookie Nicholas Singleton some playing time.

injuries.shortComment: Ayomanor caught all three of his targets for 27 yards in Sunday's loss to Dallas.
injuries.longComment: Ayomanor logged season highs with five catches, 10 targets and 79 yards against Jacksonville in Week 10, but he reverted back closer to his usual numbers versus the Cowboys. The second-year wideout did rank third on the team in receptions and receiving yards, and his 37 offensive snaps also were third behind Carnell Tate (62) and Chimere Dike (54). Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) is out for the remainder of the season, but Ayomanor may be hard-pressed to put up reliable fantasy production as the third pass-catching option, at best, for one of the league's least prolific air attacks.

injuries.shortComment: Slye made all three field-goal attempts and went 3-for-3 on PATs in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.
injuries.longComment: The veteran kicker made field goals from 38, 48 and 28 yards in the first half and is in the midst of a career-best season. He's now 18-for-19 on field-goal tries and has made all 17 PATs through 10 games. Kicking in one of the lower-scoring offenses in the league, it still doesn't translate to much fantasy appeal for Slye ahead of next Sunday's road date with the Jaguars.

injuries.shortComment: Helm caught two of three targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.
injuries.longComment: The tight end has yet to catch a touchdown this season and was unable to get anything going against arguably the league's worst defense Sunday. Helm has been held below 30 receiving yards in nine of 10 games this season. He's nothing more than a low-end TE2 in fantasy.

injuries.shortComment: Dike caught six of seven targets for 69 yards during Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.
injuries.longComment: Dike was able to reel in multiple passes for the third straight game, and his six snags set a new season high for the second-year pro. The 24-year-old paced the team in targets Sunday, narrowly edging out fellow wide receivers Calvin Ridley (six) and Carnell Tate (five). Dike will have a chance to continue carving out a more substantial role for himself on offense moving forward with Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) sidelined for the rest of the 2026 campaign.

injuries.shortComment: Ridley caught five of six targets for 68 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.
injuries.longComment: Ridley reeled in multiple passes in a contest for the first time since Week 5, and his 12-yard touchdown connection with Cam Ward in the fourth quarter was the wideout's first score of the year. Ridley trailed only fellow wide receiver Chimere Dike (seven) in targets, and Ridley could continue to see added opportunities moving forward with Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) sidelined for the remainder of the 2026 campaign.

injuries.shortComment: Ward completed 21 of 30 passes for 248 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing twice for three yards and another score in the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
injuries.longComment: Ward's final line belies his struggles somewhat, as a Cowboys defense that made a defensive playcaller switch brought him down for five sacks and forced a lost fumble on one of them at Dallas' 20-yard line. Ward did manage to connect with Carnell Tate (59 yards) and Calvin Ridley (12 yards) for his pair of TD passes, the first coming when the rookie wideout alertly got up after not being touched and the second on a broken play where Ward threw across the field after buying several extra seconds with his legs. Ward also had a one-yard touchdown run in the third quarter, and despite Tennessee's team-level misery, the second-year signal-caller has thrown for at least 231 yards and two touchdowns in three consecutive games heading into a Week 12 road matchup against the Jaguars next Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Tate brought in two of five targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Tate had a fairly non-descript day overall despite the Titans' 30-point output, but he rewarded fantasy managers with a 59-yard catch-and run touchdown in the third quarter on which he alertly got up and ran down the left sideline after Cowboys defenders failed to touch him while he was down. The rookie fourth overall pick was making his return from a two-game absence due to a shoulder injury, and the score served as Tate's second of his career, both which have come in his last three games. Tate has at least 58 receiving yards in five of the last six contests, including in three straight, heading into a Week 12 road matchup against the Jaguars next Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Pollard rushed 21 times for 110 yards and failed to bring in his only target in the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Pollard eclipsed the century mark on the ground for the third time in the last four games, lighting up his old team for multiple productive gains on the afternoon. The veteran back has been a bright spot in a dismal 1-9 start for Tennessee, despite game script often working against the ground attack in the second halves of the Titans' contests. Pollard remains firmly on pace for a fifth straight 1,000-yard season heading into a Week 12 road matchup against the Jaguars next Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Diggs (personal) was removed from the Commanders' injury report Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Diggs had an excused absence Wednesday but avoided the injury report entirely one day later, setting him up to continue to serve as Washington's clear-cut No. 1 wide receiver. Since Terry McLaurin was lost for the season due to a torn patellar tendon that he suffered in Week 6 at San Francisco, Diggs has compiled a 16-217-2 line on 27 targets over the last four games.

injuries.shortComment: Burks (foot) was listed as limited on Thursday's injury report.
injuries.longComment: Burks has been listed on Commanders practice reports with a foot injury since Week 8, but he's missed only one contest (Week 9 against the Rams) in four chances during that span. Friday's report will determine if Burks has a designation ahead of Sunday's contest at Arizona.

injuries.shortComment: Robertson (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.longComment: Robertson was unable to play against the Bengals on Monday due to an ankle injury that he picked up during Friday's practice. He would need to log a limited session over the next two days to have a chance at playing against the Cardinals on Sunday.

injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: Bates didn't garner a target during Monday night's 22-20 win over the Bengals.
injuries.longComment: Bates went without a target for the fourth straight game. The 29-year-old's 21 offensive snaps ranked third at tight end behind Chig Okonkwo (49) and Ben Sinnott (24), and Bates should continue to have no fantasy value in Week 12 versus the Cardinals.

injuries.shortComment: Sinnott played played 33 snaps (24 on offense, nine on special teams) but didn't show up in the box score otherwise during the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday.
injuries.longComment: Chig Okonkwo was the Commanders' only tight end who produced offensively Monday, with the fifth-year pro catching four of five passes for 66 yards. Sinnott has been targeted zero times in seven of 10 regular-season games, with his lone productive outing being Week 10 against the Giants, when he brought in all four of his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown. He brings very little fantasy appeal heading into Washington's Week 12 road tilt against Arizona on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Jefferson failed to haul in his lone target during the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday.
injuries.longComment: Jefferson could not hold onto a deep pass from Jayden Daniels early in the fourth quarter, and that catch would have set up the Commanders in the red zone. Jefferson has seen only one pass across his two outings since putting together a 5-58-1 receiving line on seven targets against the Rams in Week 9. Jefferson is firmly entrenched as the Commanders' WR4 behind Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams and Treylon Burks heading into Week 12 against the Cardinals on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Stevens went 5-for-5 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Monday night's 22-20 win over the Bengals.
injuries.longComment: Stevens had himself a career night in Week 11. The kicker made all five field goals in the second half, converting attempts from 36, 40, 25 and 41 yards before nailing a 26-yard game winner as time expired in regulation. Stevens has now gone 22-for-25 on field-goal tries, including 4-for-7 from 50-plus yards, while making 16 of 19 extra-point attempts over the first 10 games of his rookie campaign.

injuries.shortComment: Ekeler turned seven carries into 41 yards and caught two of three targets for three yards during the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday.
injuries.longComment: Jacory Croskey-Merritt returned from a four-game absence due to a groin injury and finished Monday's game with 13 carries for 54 yards. Despite his return, Ekeler ended up with the second-most carries on the Commanders while Rachaad White -- who led Washington's backfield in Croskey-Merritt's absence -- didn't get a single touch on offense. It appears as though Ekeler is the preferred change-of-pace back in Washington's offense heading into Week 12 against Arizona.

injuries.shortComment: White turned two kickoff returns into 48 yards during Monday's 22-20 win over the Bengals.
injuries.longComment: With Jacory Croskey-Merritt back from a four-game absence due to a groin injury, White saw a season-low 15 snaps on offense, and the latter's lone carry early in the fourth quarter was nullified by a defensive offside penalty. Croskey-Merritt and Austin Ekeler were responsible for 20 of the Commanders' 26 rushing attempts Monday, and it looks like the return of the former has squeezed White out of the offensive gameplan. The Commanders will hit the road for each of their next two games, starting with Sunday against the Cardinals.

injuries.shortComment: Okonkwo brought in four of five targets for 66 yards in the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday night.
injuries.longComment: Okonkwo contributed his game-long 32-yard grab on his first catch of the night, and the veteran tight end went on to finish second in receiving yards for the Commanders. He also contributed a key 13-yard grab on Washington's penultimate drive that culminated in a key field goal, and in all, three of his four receptions resulted in first downs. Okonkwo has at least four catches in three straight games but still is seeking his first touchdown of the season heading into a Week 12 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Williams brought in nine of 11 targets for 122 yards in the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday night.
injuries.longComment: The rookie third-round pick managed new career highs across all three components of his receiving line, which also all served as team-best totals Monday. Williams' last two catches of the night were his most critical, as he recorded 22- and 42-yard grabs on Washington's final drive to position Drew Stevens for a game-winning 26-yard field goal. Williams hadn't topped 54 receiving yards in any game after a 64-yard effort in his pro debut in Week 1, but Monday night's breakout could serve as a launchpad to a strong stretch run as the Commanders make a playoff push.

injuries.shortComment: Croskey-Merritt rushed 13 times for 54 yards and a touchdown and brought in two of three targets for 23 yards in the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday night.
injuries.longComment: Making his return from a four-game absence due to a groin injury, Croskey-Merritt outpaced Austin Ekeler, the only other Commanders back to log a carry, by six rush attempts. The second-year pro also recorded his third rushing touchdown of the season on a one-yard run with 12 seconds remaining in the first half. Croskey-Merritt averaged over 4.0 yards per carry for the second straight game after failing to eclipse that mark in each of the first four games of the season, and he should be in store for an even busier day in a favorable Week 12 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Daniels completed 23 of 35 passes for 289 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and added six carries for 55 yards in the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday night.
injuries.longComment: Daniels looked like he was on his way to a middling night during a first half in which he led the Commanders to just seven points, but the 2024 first-round pick flipped a switch in the second half, particularly in the fourth quarter. Daniels led field-goal drives of 13, 11 and five plays that netted a total of 193 yards during the final period, the last one featuring strikes of 22 and 42 yards to Antonio Williams to position Drew Stevens for a game-winning field goal. Daniels finished with his second-highest passing yardage total of the season, and he also mustered his seventh interception-free effort of the campaign. Having helped Washington to a critical victory, he'll look to carry the momentum over into a favorable Week 12 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Patrick (concussion) is active for Monday night's game against the Bengals.
injuries.longComment: Patrick has cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol in time for Monday night's contest. Patrick will step back into his starting center role against an improved Bengals defensive line.

injuries.shortComment: Martin (shoulder) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Bengals.
injuries.longComment: Martin's practice reps were limited both Thursday and Friday due to a shoulder issue, but his full session Saturday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Monday night's game. Martin could see an uptick in defensive snaps if defensive back Amik Robertson (ankle) is not cleared to play against Cincinnati.

injuries.shortComment: Tunsil (triceps) is progressing well in his recovery but is not expected to return by the end of the 2026 regular season, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports.
injuries.longComment: Tunsil underwent surgery in August to repair a torn triceps. The left tackle continues to recover, but he likely will not suit up for the Commanders in 2026 unless the team makes a playoff run. Even then, it remains unclear whether Tunsil would be able to return at all before the 2027 season.

injuries.shortComment: Yankoff (knee) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Yankoff sat out the Commanders' contest against the Giants in Week 10 because of a knee injury, but it now looks like he's put it behind him. He figures to resume a depth role at tight end in Week 11 against the Bengals.

injuries.shortComment: McCaffrey returned two punts for 13 yards and three kickoffs for 58 yards in Thursday's 24-21 win over the Giants.
injuries.longComment: Though he's been active for five straight games while the Commanders' receiving depth has taken hits due to season-ending injuries to Terry McLaurin (knee) and Jaylin Lane (ankle), McCaffrey has yet to carve out much of a role on offense. He took the field for a season-high 14 of the Commanders' 69 offensive plays in Week 10 but went without a target. McCaffrey is likely to continue to provide his greatest impact on special teams, where he appears to have settled in as the Commanders' top return man on both kickoffs and punts.

injuries.shortComment: Reaves recorded nine tackles (seven solo), one pass defense and one fumble recovery during the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Reaves finished Thursday's game second on the Commanders in tackles behind rookie first-round linebacker Sonny Styles (13), and the former jumped on a loose ball caused by Frankie Luvu in the third quarter that stopped the Giants' red zone drive. Reaves has logged at least five stops in each of the first nine games of the regular season, and the veteran safety is up to 62 tackles (35 solo), four pass defenses and one fumble recovery on the year.

injuries.shortComment: Cross finished Thursday's 24-21 win over the Giants with six tackles (one solo).
injuries.longComment: Cross was one of three Commanders players who played all 65 defensive snaps during Thursday's win. He's posted at least six stops in each of his last three outings, and over that span, he has accumulated 23 tackles (12 solo), three pass defenses (including one interception) and one fumble recovery.
